sanskrit:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम्।
मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्।।
image_english: I am the ritual, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the chant, the butter, the fire, and the offering.
caption:
Chapter 9, Verse 16

Kṛṣṇa declares His identity with the Vedic ritual. ‘ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ’ (I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice). ‘svadhāham’ (I am the offering to the ancestors). ‘aham auṣadham’ (I am the healing herb). ‘mantro ’ham’ (I am the transcendental chant). ‘aham evājyam’ (I am the butter). ‘aham agnir’ (I am the fire). ‘ahaṁ hutam’ (I am the act of offering). In a yajña, everything is Kṛṣṇa. The priest, the fire, the ghee, the mantra, and the fruit—all are manifestations of His energy. Therefore, the Bhakta doesn’t need to perform separate rituals; by worshiping Kṛṣṇa, he has already performed every yajña.
